# Recording and AI Notice

Version 2026-11-19 · **A first draft, not yet reviewed by a lawyer.**

What happens to a recorded KT session, who sees it, and what the host must do before recording.

**For:** Everyone who takes part in a KT session, and everyone who adds a recording\
**Accepted by:** Each person, for themselves, in the product.

## In brief

- KT sessions in your organisation may be recorded and added to Welcome Wave, so that colleagues who join later can learn from them.
- A recording holds your voice, your face if your camera is on, and anything shared on screen. An AI model watches it to write a transcript and notes.
- Members of the project can watch it, and the assistant can use what was said to answer them. Managers and admins can open the full transcript.
- You can say no before a session, and you can ask for a recording to be removed afterwards.
- The host must tell everyone before recording starts and get their agreement. Some places make that the law.

## 1. What is recorded

Welcome Wave does not record calls. A session is recorded by the meeting tool your organisation uses, such as Google Meet. The file reaches Welcome Wave in one of two ways: a member adds it, or Welcome Wave brings it in from your organisation's Google Drive when the session was booked through its Google Calendar. Neither happens until a member has confirmed that everyone agreed (section 7).

A recording holds what the meeting tool captured: voices, faces if cameras were on, shared screens, and whatever was said or shown.

## 2. Why

To pass knowledge on. A recorded explanation becomes notes, a searchable transcript and clips placed beside the code they explain. Answers to colleagues' questions can cite it, and the gaps it leaves help plan further sessions.

## 3. What the AI does

One of Google's Gemini models receives the recording, picture and sound. It writes a transcript that says who spoke, notes with decisions and action items, descriptions of what was on screen, and links to the code that was discussed. It labels a speaker it cannot name as “Speaker 1”, “Speaker 2”.

Before any of that text is stored, a redactor replaces email addresses, phone numbers, common key formats and password-like values with labels.

> **What redaction does not do.** The redactor follows patterns. It does not remove names, voices or faces, it can miss things, and the video file itself is stored as recorded. If something was said or shown that should not be kept, ask for the recording to be removed.

Welcome Wave makes no voiceprints and no face templates, and does not use a recording to identify people by their body or voice.

We do not train AI models on recordings. Google handles what it receives under its own terms: [Privacy Policy](PRIVACY.md), section 5, explains them, including the difference between free and paid Gemini API keys.

The project's managers are asked to review the notes of each recorded session.

## 4. Who can see it

- **Members of the project.** They can watch the recording and read the notes. Clips appear beside the code they explain and as sources in answers. The assistant reads passages of the transcript to write those answers, so an answer can repeat what someone said.
- **Managers and admins.** They can also open the full transcript.
- **Admins.** They can export the organisation's records, which include transcripts and notes but not the video file.
- **Outside your organisation.** Nobody can see any of it. The people who run the servers can technically reach the files, and do so only when it is needed to run, secure or support the service.

## 5. How long it is kept

- **The video file.** On Google Cloud it is deleted automatically after 30 days. On a single server it is deleted after the number of days the operator has set, or kept until someone removes it when no period is set.
- **Notes, transcript and links to code.** Until a manager removes them or the organisation is deleted.
- **Google's copy for analysis.** On a single server, the recording is uploaded to Google for the AI to read. Welcome Wave deletes that copy when the analysis finishes or fails. A copy it could not delete is removed by Google within 48 hours of the upload.
- **Tracing, only when the operator has turned it on.** Text from the transcript, after redaction, is part of what LangSmith receives. LangSmith keeps it for its own period, and removing a recording here does not remove it there.
- **Backups.** Deleted records stay in a backup until that backup expires.

> **On this service.** In the product, this place says how the service you are reading it on is set up: where it runs, how long a recording's video file is kept and whether tracing is on.

## 6. Saying no, and having a recording removed

You can decline to be recorded. Tell the host before the session. A session can be held, and kept in Welcome Wave, with no recording.

Afterwards, you can ask for a recording to be removed: on the session's page, or by asking a project manager or your admin. A manager then removes the video, the transcript, the notes, the links to code and the search entries in one step, or declines with a reason. You are told either way. Answers that cited a removed recording are marked out of date. The confirmation that everyone agreed is cleared with the recording, so adding it again needs a new one.

Your organisation decides on a request, because it is responsible for the recording. If it does not answer, write to the privacy contact for this service and we pass your request on.

## 7. If you host or record a session

Before recording starts:

1. Tell every participant that the session will be recorded, including guests from outside your organisation.
2. Say that the recording goes into Welcome Wave, that AI writes a transcript and notes from it, and that colleagues on the project can watch it.
3. Get everyone's agreement. Some countries and some US states require the agreement of every person on a call, and recording without it can be an offence. If you are not sure which rule applies, get everyone's agreement.
4. If someone does not agree, do not record, or let them leave first.

> **Words you can use.** “This session is being recorded. The recording will be kept in Welcome Wave, where AI writes notes and a transcript for colleagues on this project. Is everyone happy to continue?”

The calendar invitation for a session booked through Welcome Wave says that it will be recorded, what to do if you do not agree, and where to read this notice.

When a recording is added, a member confirms that every participant was told and agreed. Welcome Wave keeps who confirmed, when, and which version of this notice applied. Without that confirmation it refuses the recording.

Welcome Wave cannot see who was in a call. The confirmation is that member's own statement, so make it only when it is true.

## 8. Your acknowledgement

Each member is asked to acknowledge this notice once, and again when it changes. Acknowledging it means you have read it. It is not your agreement to any particular recording: that is asked for before each session.

## 9. Questions

Ask your organisation's admin, or write to the privacy contact for this service.
